t: The Signature Vision: Mile-High Vertical Cities
title: The Signature Vision: Mile-High Vertical Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Mile-High Vertical Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Mile-High Vertical Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature mile hulls program, charter one: master vertical districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale elevator transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate structural cores systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Mile-High Vertical Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

t: 2030 — The first mile hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first mile hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Mile-High Vertical Cities roadmap.
description:
The first mile hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its vertical districts grid and elevator transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the vertical districts results have to replicate outside the lab, elevator transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and structural cores operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed vertical districts demonstrations, elevator transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting structural cores uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

Depends on: vertical districts, elevator transit, structural cores.

title: Readiness Estimator: Mile-High Vertical Cities
definition: Estimates Mile-High Vertical Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Mile-High Vertical Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a mile hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Mile-High Vertical Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Mile-High Vertical Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Mile-High Vertical Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 15564 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where vertical districts monitoring, elevator transit redundancy, or structural cores maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Mile-High Vertical Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Mile-High Vertical Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Mile-High Vertical Cities — single structures a mile tall functioning as cities.

Phase 1 — Prove (vertical districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (elevator transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (structural cores): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (sky neighborhoods): mile hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and urban core-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
